hypothesis: After E6's complete bytecode, the cold init's main thread still imports numpy (86 modules), pydantic (38), tokenizers (14) and strands_decider before PR #77's background load starts the S3 download. None of them is needed before the download starts. Importing them inside the load, beside the download, makes the main-thread `imports` phase and REPORT Init Duration shorter (expected < 50 ms) and starts the download earlier, with no change to answers. The cold first request is not expected to improve while the ~25 s download is the binding constraint (E6).

conclusion: Moving the model-stack import (engine: numpy, pydantic, tokenizers, strands_decider) off the init's main thread and into the load, beside the S3 download, cuts what it targets on every CPU part Lambda gave us, matched by part, both arms in every wave: cold `imports` 0.367 -> 0.004 s on 0xd40 (delta -0.364 s, 95% CI [-0.371, -0.356], n=51/44; 0xd4f -0.281 s [-0.284, -0.275], n=26/30; 0xd0c -0.558 s, n=3/6) and REPORT Init Duration 0.477 -> 0.123 s on 0xd40 (-0.354 s [-0.367, -0.338]; 0xd4f -0.283 s [-0.303, -0.274]; 0xd0c -0.559 s, n=3/6). That is about 7x the < 50 ms the card expected: on Lambda the import costs 0.28-0.56 s even with E6's bytecode, against 0.12-0.13 s offline. All 8 0xd40 and 7 0xd4f cold-imports cells are below 0 beyond the control spread. The download starts 0.36 s earlier (load_start 0.369 -> 0.006 s on 0xd40). The cold first request does NOT change on 0xd40 (-0.023 s [-0.067, +0.044]) or 0xd4f (-0.055 s [-0.123, +0.035]). The engine import still runs before the load needs it, now beside the download (0.74 s on 0xd40 on its own thread, against 0.36 s on the main thread: the two compete for the GIL and cores), and the download ends at the same time (start + download 25.80 vs 25.80 s on 0xd40, -0.004 s [-0.027, +0.018]), so the model is ready at the same time (35.79 vs 35.77 s). The download is the binding constraint, as in E6. 0xd0c (n=3/6) shows -0.66 s on the first request, but the sample is too small for a claim. Billed cold Duration is unchanged (36.14 vs 36.12 s p50 on 0xd40): the Init saved is spent waiting inside Duration. Restore (0xd40, n=29/21) +0.076 s [-0.011, +0.143] and warm (0xd40, n=284/241) +0.005 s [-0.020, +0.021]: unchanged. The SnapStart snapshot init (publish time, not on any request path) finishes the load 0.74 s sooner by median on 0xd40 (model_ready 69.95 -> 69.21 s, 3 versions per arm; one lazy version, 70.43 s, was slower than every e6 version). Answers: 540/540 lazy answers bit-identical to e6's for the same request and CPU part; all 856 answers P1's reference covers bit-identical to it. 0 errors, 0 class mismatches in 1,080 invocations. Detection floor on 0xd40 Init Duration: CI half-width 14 ms. Cost $1.94 (ceiling $10). Status no-change by the headline rule. Recommendation: adopt as a candidate ladder rung for R/S/G. It costs nothing and is a measured 0.28-0.56 s cut in Init Duration and in time to download start. It pays off on the first request only on a rung where the download is no longer the critical path (E4 streaming, E3, or a smaller/faster weight fetch). There, re-measure it, because the off-thread import then competes with the load.

host_variability.method: Within each observed CPU part, compare arm medians in each round. Arms are sequential waves whose first position alternates by round; this is alternation, not within-round interleaving. A directional effect must exceed the control observations' within-cell range in every assessed shared cell; deltas inside that range support a null outcome even if their signs vary. Every shared cell persists its own outcome (within-control-variation, negative- or positive-beyond-control-variation, or unassessed), and each CPU part's outcome is aggregated from those persisted cell outcomes. A cell with fewer than two control observations has no spread estimate and is explicitly unassessed, but its observed sign is kept: an opposite sign on an unassessed cell makes its CPU part host-conditioned even when the part's assessed cells agree, and an opposite sign on a wholly unassessed part blocks a comparable directional outcome. Missing-arm cells and rows without CPU identity are listed but never treated as comparable strata.

primary_effect.reason: every assessed cell has a negative delta whose absolute size exceeds its control within-cell spread; sparse cells and CPU parts are unassessed and have no opposite observed sign

assessment.deployment_headlines: no consistent cold-first-request, restore, or warm benefit across observed CPU parts and rounds
assessment.rerun: not needed: host-adjusted assessed cells support one imports-phase outcome; sparse CPU parts and unmatched cells remain explicit limitations, while deployment headlines remain null

assessment.reason: every assessed CPU part has the same outcome against its control spread across published versions; sparse CPU parts have no opposite-sign observation; missing, ambiguous and unpublished records are excluded and counted

snapshot_init.method: Each before_snapshot record is bound to the CPU part named by the `decider.engine init cpu_part=` line in its own log stream (one stream = one execution environment); binding never crosses streams. Only streams of versions this run published count. A stream with no known part is missing, one with more than one distinct part is ambiguous; neither is a comparison stratum. Within each CPU part, the pyc-minus-ctl median delta across published versions is judged against the range of ctl's per-version values (cell_outcome); a part with fewer than two control inits is unassessed, and an opposite observed sign on such a sparse part blocks a comparable directional outcome.
limits: snapshot inits run inside publish_version, so this is publish time, not a request-path latency

only the CPU part is observable for a snapshot init (the engine's init log line); variant, revision, HWCAP, features, CPU count and kernel come from e6_entry's first-invocation record, which a snapshot init does not emit, so they are unknown here
availability zone, physical host and cgroup limits are unknown
Lambda chose which CPU parts to prepare per version; one init per (version, part, arm), so spread is across versions, not within a version
no Graviton generation is inferred from the CPU part

delta.method: lazy minus e6, medians within each CPU part both arms ran on; ci95 = bootstrap over environments (4,000 resamples, seed 6); both arms ran in every wave (interleaved); pooled per-round deltas are descriptive only; host_variability contains the round-by-CPU-part cells

download_completion.method:
weight_download alone is not comparable between arms: lazy's download starts earlier. load_start + the load's
    pre-download time + weight_download is. Here, from each environment's init record:
      pre_download   model_ready - engine_load - warmup_inference - weight_download (the load's time before the
                     download returned that was not the download: on lazy, the wait for the engine import)
      download_done  load_start + model_ready - engine_load - warmup_inference
      ready          load_start + model_ready
    lazy minus e6 medians per CPU part, bootstrap 95 % CI over environments.

host.note: baseline/hostinfo.py (H1) read inside the function at init and again after a restore. A null field or an `unknown` key was not exposed. No processor generation is inferred from a CPU part or a timing.

arm_agreement.method: complete answer object of every successful pyc invocation vs the ctl answer for the same request id and CPU part in this run
